propositions.text: The claimant is Ms. XXXX XXXX, a 59-year-old Pakistani citizen seeking protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97.
propositions.quote: The claimant is Ms. XXXX XXXX who is a 59 year old citizen of Pakistan. Ms. XXXX is seeking protection in Canada citing Sections 96 and 97 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).

paragraphs.summary: The court states the claimant is a 59-year-old Pakistani woman seeking protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97.

propositions.text: The claimant alleges she was targeted due to her Ahmadi Muslim faith by an extremist named Mr. XXX and his organization.
propositions.quote: Ms. XXXX alleges that because of her faith, which is Ahmadi Muslim, she has been targeted by 'XXXX' XXXX XXX who is an extremist XXXX at a nearby Mosque and XXXX of the local Aahafaz Khateme Nabuwat organization.

propositions.text: The organization has a history of targeting and persecuting Ahmadi Muslims.
propositions.quote: This organization has a history of targeting and persecuting Ahmadi Muslims.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges she was targeted by an extremist and his organization known for persecuting Ahmadi Muslims.

propositions.text: The claimant alleges she hosted events at her house for local women.
propositions.quote: The claimant alleges that she regularly hosted 'events' at her house. For example, she would have local woman over to XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX.

propositions.text: She alleges she was appointed 'XXXX XXXX' of her local Jamaat's Lajna (Ahmadi Women's Organization) and was involved in its activities.
propositions.quote: Ms. XXXX also alleges that she was appointed 'XXXX XXXX' of her local Jamaat's Lajna (Ahmadi Women's Organization) and therefore she was involved in XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges she hosted women's events and was appointed to a leadership role in the local Ahmadi women's organization.

propositions.text: In 2007, Mr. XXX accused the claimant of organizing Ahmadi religious activities and teaching Quran to Sunni children.
propositions.quote: The claimant alleges that in XXXX 2007 Mr. XXX mentioned the claimant XXXX XXXX. Mr. XXX charged the claimant with "actively organising Ahmadi religious activities in my house and was teaching Quran (Ahmadi version) to Sunni children".

propositions.text: Four of Mr. XXX's 'hooligans' damaged her satellite dish the following week.
propositions.quote: The next week the claimant alleges that four of Mr. XXX's "hooligans" damaged her satellite dish.

propositions.text: Police refused to help after discovering the claimant was Ahmadi, deeming it a religious problem.
propositions.quote: The claimant asked for police help but when they discovered that the claimants were Ahmadi they determined that it was a religious problem and they refused to help.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges Mr. XXX accused her of religious activities, his followers damaged her property, and police refused help due to religion.

propositions.text: The claimant received threatening calls and friends were harassed; she was personally threatened by Mr. XXX.
propositions.quote: Soon the claimant was receiving threatening phone calls and some of the claimant's friends were harassed. The claimant was then personally threatened by Mr. XXXX.

propositions.text: On XXXX 2007, Mr. XXX protested outside her house during a women's meeting and announced a death verdict against her.
propositions.quote: The most serious incident occurred on XXXX, 2007 when the claimant had XX women at her house for an annual Lajna Tarbyati meeting. XXXX XXXX XXX with several followers protested outside and the woman needed to be escorted home for their own protection. According to the claimant, "XXXX verbally announced death verdict against me".

propositions.text: The claimant hid and later fled Pakistan to Canada on her husband's advice.
propositions.quote: The claimant then hid in another part of XXXX. After consideration the claimant fled Pakistan to arrive in Canada on the advice of her husband.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges threats, a death verdict announced at her home, and that she fled Pakistan to Canada on her husband's advice.

propositions.text: The panel determines the claimant is not a convention refugee under section 96 of IRPA.
propositions.quote: The panel determines that Ms. XXXX is not a "convention refugee" under section 96 of IRPA.

propositions.text: The claimant is not a person in need of protection under section 97(1)(a) or (b) of IRPA.
propositions.quote: The claimant is also not a person "in need of protection" within the meaning of section 97(1)(a) or (b) of IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claimant is neither a convention refugee nor in need of protection under IRPA sections 96 or 97.

propositions.text: The panel is satisfied as to the claimant's identity based on passport and marriage certificate.
propositions.quote: The panel is satisfied as to the identity of the claimant. The panel was provided a passport and marriage certificate for review.

paragraphs.summary: The panel confirms the claimant's identity from passport and marriage certificate.

propositions.text: The panel does not find the claimant credible due to vagueness, implausibility, and evasiveness.
propositions.quote: With respect to credibility the panel does not find the claimant is telling the truth. There are aspects of the claim which are vague or lacking in plausibility. At times the claimant was evasive.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claimant not credible due to vague, implausible, and evasive testimony.

propositions.text: The basic allegation of targeting by Mr. XXX is possible but many indicators suggest fabrication.
propositions.quote: The basic allegation that the claimant was targeted by 'XXXX' XXXX XXX is possible. At the same time there are numerous indicators that the claim is a fabrication.

propositions.text: CIC received information from claimant's former son-in-law in 2006 that claimant planned to claim asylum in Canada.
propositions.quote: before the claimant arrived in Canada, CIC received information from the claimant's former son in law that the claimant was planning to make a refugee claim in Canada.

propositions.text: Mr. XXXX XXXX XXXX stated claimant planned to apply for asylum upon arrival in Canada.
propositions.quote: According to Mr. XXXX XXXX XXXX the claimant was going to "apply the visit visa for Canada and upon arrival here in Canada she will apply for asylum (refugee) for getting immigration, as they plan together".

propositions.text: This communication was received in XXXX 2006.
propositions.quote: This communication was received on XXXX, 2006.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the targeting claim possible but notes CIC received info in 2006 that claimant planned asylum claim in Canada.

propositions.text: The claimant did not claim refugee status after arriving in Canada in 2006, stayed 4 months, then returned to Pakistan.
propositions.quote: In fact the claimant did not claim refugee status after arrival in Canada in XXXX 2006. The claimant stayed in Canada for 4 months and returned to Pakistan in XXXX.

propositions.text: The claimant alleges she was targeted upon return to Pakistan and made a refugee claim upon returning to Canada in 2007.
propositions.quote: The claimant alleges, however, that upon return to Pakistan she was soon being targeted by Mr. XXX and as a result, on her return to Canada in XXXX 2007, she did make a refugee claim.

paragraphs.summary: The panel notes claimant did not claim refugee status in 2006 but alleges targeting upon return to Pakistan and claims refugee status in 2007.

propositions.text: The claimant argues Mr. XXX was resentful over her daughter's failed marriage and was lying about predicting her refugee claim.
propositions.quote: The claimant argues that Mr. XXXX was resentful over the failed marriage with her daughter. The claimant states that he was "lying" about what the claimant said

propositions.text: The claimant argues her return to Pakistan in 2006 disproves Mr. XXX's prediction.
propositions.quote: the claimant argues that because she in fact returned to Pakistan in 2006 provides evidence of this.

propositions.text: The panel concludes that despite animosity, Mr. XXX was essentially correct in predicting the refugee claim.
propositions.quote: The panel concludes that although a marriage breakdown may create animosity, this does not detract from the fact that Mr. XXXX was essentially correct in his prediction.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant argues Mr. XXX lied about predicting her refugee claim; the panel finds he was essentially correct despite animosity.

propositions.text: The claimant could not provide evidence of Mr. XXX's existence and was vague about his mosque's location.
propositions.quote: The claimant was asked to provide any evidence of the existence of Mr. XXX. The claimant could not. ... The claimant was very vague on the location of Mr. XXX's mosque.

propositions.text: The claimant gave confused and evasive answers about the mosque's location and name.
propositions.quote: The claimant gave a confused answer. The claimant stated that Mr. XXX's Mosque was in the XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX but was evasive about the specific location speaking first about it being in an adjacent town then about it being in a 'border' area. The claimant could also not give the name of the Mosque where Mr. XXX XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claimant gave no evidence of Mr. XXX's existence and was vague and evasive about his mosque's location and name.

propositions.text: The claimant's answers are unsatisfactory given her long residence, education, and resources.
propositions.quote: Panel does not find these answers satisfactory. The claimant has lived in this house in XXX since 1996. The claimant is an educated woman from a family of professionals. She has access to financial resources.

propositions.text: The claimant provided no documentary evidence of Mr. XXX or the events described.
propositions.quote: Regardless, the claimant has provided no documentary evidence of the existence of Mr. XXX or of any of the events described.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claimant's unsatisfactory answers and lack of documentary evidence implausible given her background and resources.

propositions.text: The claimant was vague about her Lajna involvement and could only name the president by first name.
propositions.quote: The claimant was also vague about her involvement in the Lajna organization. ... she states that the president appointed her. At the same time the claimant could only identify the president by a first name.

propositions.text: She lacked knowledge of other organizational roles and members, including those present during the alleged attack.
propositions.quote: The claimant also appears to lack knowledge of organizational activities of the Lajna. ... The claimant could not name other members of the organization or even give the names of individuals who were at her house on XXXX, 2007 when her house was allegedly attacked by Mr. XXX and his supporters.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claimant vague about her Lajna role and lacking knowledge of members and events during the alleged attack.

propositions.text: The claimant's status as 'XXXX XXXX' was first mentioned in a 2008 amendment, not in the original PIF narrative.
propositions.quote: The panel also notes that the claimant's status as an 'XXXX XXXX' is first mentioned in an amendment to the PIF Narrative received in XXXX 2008. The original PIF narrative gives a rendition of events which implies that the claimant was not involved in any structured events.

propositions.text: The claimant states the Lajna monthly gatherings were regular events at her house.
propositions.quote: According to the claimant: The monthly gathering of the Lajna (Ahmadi women organization) was a regular event at my house XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX

paragraphs.summary: The panel notes the claimant first mentioned her Lajna role in a 2008 amendment; claimant says monthly gatherings were regular at her house.

propositions.text: The claimant did not explain why her official Lajna role was omitted from earlier documents.
propositions.quote: The claimant did not provide a response to the question of why there was no prior mention of her official role in the Lajna in the Port of Entry documentation or the PIF Narrative.

paragraphs.summary: The panel notes the claimant did not explain omission of her Lajna role from earlier documents.

propositions.text: It is implausible the claimant could not get police protection in a prosperous, militarily secured area.
propositions.quote: In addition the panel also finds it implausible that the claimant could not receive some form of police protection. The area that the claimant lived in is a very prosperous area and the security is provided by the military.

propositions.text: The claimant's husband is a retired military officer and her son is active military.
propositions.quote: The claimant's husband is a retired XXXX in the military and one of her sons is an active service XXXX stationed in XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds it implausible the claimant lacked police protection in a prosperous, militarily secured area where her husband and son serve.

propositions.text: A brochure describes the claimant's area as a secure, prosperous community with many amenities.
propositions.quote: according to the brochure promoting sales of new properties in the area, "Home to many, XXXX XXXX XXXX (XXX) is a residential Paradise, a cultural heartland and a land of endless opportunities...

propositions.text: There is a police station at the end of the claimant's block in XXX.
propositions.quote: With respect to where the claimant lives in XXX, there is a police station at the end of the block.

propositions.text: The area does not appear to allow religious extremists to harass citizens or damage property as alleged.
propositions.quote: From the appearance of XXX this does not appear to be a place where a religious extremist and 'hooligans' would be allowed to do as they please in terms of roughing up citizens, damaging private property (damage to the satellite dish) and protesting in the neighborhood.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claimant's area is secure with police presence and unlikely to allow extremist harassment as alleged.

propositions.text: The claimant's family continued living in the house after she fled, suggesting security in the area.
propositions.quote: the claimant's son along with his wife and family continued to live in the house after the claimant fled. There are also servants who have lived continuously at the house. The claimant's husband also lives there when he is in XXXX. The claimant's daughter, XXXX, who was formally in Canada and with whom the claimant was living, has returned to Pakistan and lives in the house.

propositions.text: The claimant's daughter returned to Pakistan for social reasons despite alleged targeting of the claimant.
propositions.quote: The claimant was asked why her daughter returned to Pakistan. The claimant replied that she wanted to see her friends again and was bored.

propositions.text: The family's behavior suggests substantial security despite the claimant's alleged targeting.
propositions.quote: Although Mr. XXX is focused on the claimant the fact remains that the claimant was targeted partly because she is Ahmadi. Yet the behaviour of this family, aside from the claimant, suggests that there is a substantial degree of security at this house.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claimant's family remained in the house, indicating security despite the claimant's alleged targeting.

propositions.text: The claimant's family is educated and professional with financial resources and properties.
propositions.quote: The panel notes that all of the claimant's family members are educated and professional. The claimant's husband is a retired XXXX who possesses a BSc. and a law degree. The claimant's eldest son, XXXX possesses an MBA and works for XXXX. The claimant's middle son, XXXX is an army XXXX. The claimant's youngest son, who lives at the house but is between jobs, has an MBA. The claimant's husband mostly lives in his home village of origin. At the same time the claimant states that her husband has family members living there and properties which provide him revenue. The claimant's husband also has people cooking and cleaning for him there.

propositions.text: The family is prosperous and secure overall.
propositions.quote: All this indicates that the family as a whole is prosperous and secure.

paragraphs.summary: The panel notes the claimant's family is educated, professional, prosperous, and secure with properties and income.

propositions.text: On a balance of probabilities the allegations of the claimant are false
propositions.quote: Taken together the panel determines that on a balance of probabilities the allegations of the claimant are false.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claimant's allegations false on a balance of probabilities.

propositions.text: The claimant is not a 'convention refugee' nor a 'person in need of protection', so the claim is denied
propositions.quote: For all of the reasons set out above this panel determines that the claimant is not a 'convention refugee' nor is she a 'person in need of protection' therefore the claim is denied.

paragraphs.summary: The panel concludes the claimant is neither a convention refugee nor in need of protection and denies the claim.
